name: Pethahiah
overview: Pethahiah was a male Levite who served as the nineteenth-chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established in ancient Israel. He belonged to the line of Eleazar, one of the sons of Aaron, indicating his priestly heritage and role within the religious leadership of Israel as recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:16.
namesAndTitles: The name Pethahiah means 'YHWH opens,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's action or provision. This proper name, as given in 1 Chronicles 24:16, does not indicate that it was divinely assigned but carries a meaning consistent with the worshipful context of his priestly service.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Pethahiah as a descendant of Eleazar, linking him to the prominent priestly family within the tribe of Levi. Beyond this lineage, no additional family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pethahiah's significance lies in his role as one of the twenty-four priestly divisions instituted to organize the service of the temple, specifically as the nineteenth leader of the courses descended from Eleazar. This organization was crucial for the orderly worship and sacrificial duties in Israel, highlighting the continuity of priestly service through generations as established by God’s appointment.
